name: playbook.decision
title: Decision

method: Treat the user's request as a choice from the first reply. Do not warm up with a briefing, a What Changed tour, or a dashboard mock unless they asked for those.

Lock the decision question in one sentence before options. If the question, the option set, or a constraint would change the pick and no high-confidence default exists, block and ask a multiple-choice Floor question. Do not invent a menu to look decisive.

Gather only the evidence that would change the pick. Put a compact comparison on Stage (one row per option or one row per thing compared). Prose does not invent a number the Stage does not show. At most one claim chart, and only if the shape is the reason to pick.
Name two to six options. Each gets a short label, what it means, and a consequence if chosen. Include wait / do nothing when that is a real path. Do not pad to six.
Recommend one option only when the evidence supports it. Say why in one or two lines. If the evidence does not pick a winner, say so and still put the choice in front of them.

Put the choice on a real control: request_calliope_input for an ordinary Decision in this chat; calliope_decision_request only when a current ranked observation is the reason for the judgment (read calliope_observation_context first, cite that observation id, do not duplicate it as a Work Inbox item). Never ask the same questions only in prose.
Chat stays short: the question, the evidence, the recommendation if any, the control. Then stop and wait. Do not keep arguing after the control is up.
Follow-ups after they pick are execution or a switch: make this a dashboard, watch it, what changed next week — not a second Decision on the same question unless they reopen it.
Stay on the thread. Do not delegate unless the user @-mentions a specialist. Cassandra, if mentioned, red-teams the same options; she does not write a parallel memo.
contract.outcome: The user makes a bounded choice with the options, consequences, and evidence in front of them — not a briefing they have to extract a decision from, and not a dashboard.
fallbacks: If they asked why it moved, run What Changed first or send them there; only switch to Decision when they want to act.
If options are still unbounded after one clarifying question, stop and ask them to name the menu rather than inventing one.
If the warehouse cannot support the comparison, say the blocker and still offer wait vs act-on-incomplete if that is honest.
If a ranked observation exists, use calliope_decision_request on that id; otherwise use request_calliope_input.
If Cassandra is @-mentioned, send the locked question, options, and evidence for critique, then integrate.
If they refuse the control and type a pick in chat, treat that as the answer and do not re-ask the same control.
If they ask to make the comparison a dashboard, switch to Dashboards and stop this method.
guardrails: Do not skip locking the question. Options without a question are not this playbook.
Do not write an essay they have to mine for a pick. The control is the deliverable.
Do not offer fewer than two or more than six options.
Do not recommend when the evidence is a tie, stale, or the wrong grain. Say the blocker.
Do not turn a What Changed claim into a Decision unless they asked to pick.
Do not use calliope_decision_request for an open-ended question, a routine update, or a generic blocker, and do not invent an observation id.
Do not put secrets, credentials, or DSNs on a Decision control.
Do not start a dashboard mock or extra charts “while we decide.”
Keep artifacts private until the user approves sharing.
Calliope stays 1:1 unless the user @-mentions a specialist.
contract.deliverable: A locked decision question, Stage evidence that would change the pick, two to six options with consequences, a recommendation only when earned, and a real in-chat choice control the user can answer or cancel.
when_to_use: The user is choosing among actions: kill or keep a channel, open a location, move budget, pick a vendor, approve or wait.
The user framed the chat as a Decision, or asked should we / pick / go or no-go / which one.
The work should end on a real choice control, not a longer analysis.
when_not_to_use: The user asked why a number moved — that is What Changed. Offer Decision only after they want to act on the claim.
The user asked for a durable dashboard or mock — that is Dashboards.
A one-number lookup, definition, or list with no choice to make.
An open-ended “what do you think” with no bounded options and no way to make two to six concrete choices.
A scheduled brief, an alert, or a data-quality repair as the primary ask.
Credentials, keys, or other secrets — never a Decision control.
context_to_gather: The decision question in one sentence: what is being picked, by when if it matters, and whose call it is.
The options the user already has in mind; do not invent a menu they did not imply unless the domain has an obvious small set.
Governed evidence that would change the pick: metric definition, window, cost, capacity, constraint. Prefer Business Context and house grain rules over reconstructing arithmetic.
Whether a ranked Calliope observation already exists for this judgment. If it does, use that observation rather than a generic choice.
What happens if they wait — delay is often a real option.
completion_criteria: The decision question is explicit in one sentence.
Two to six options are named, each with a consequence; wait is included when it is real.
Evidence that would change the pick is on Stage from executed queries or cited Brain, not invented in prose.
A recommendation is present only if the evidence supports it; otherwise the method says the evidence does not pick.
A real choice control is in the thread (request_calliope_input, or calliope_decision_request bound to an exact observation id).
Chat did not continue past the control with more analysis unless the user reopened the question.
No dashboard mock or HTML was started unless the user switched to Dashboards.
optional_capabilities: Cassandra only when @-mentioned, as a red-team of the same options.
Company Brain for a prior decision, policy, or meeting that constrains the pick.
Dashboards if they then want a durable page.
What Changed if they then want the next week's movement.
required_capabilities: Governed SQL or Business Context for evidence that would change the pick.
Stage tables (and at most one claim chart) for the comparison.
request_calliope_input for an ordinary in-chat choice.
calliope_observation_context plus calliope_decision_request when a ranked observation is the reason for the judgment.
preferred_capabilities: Library search so this Playbook is loaded instead of What Changed or Dashboards.
Local metric grain rules (events vs persons, closed periods, and the deployment's business timezone).
What Changed as a prior poke when the decision depends on a fresh delta.

synopsis: A named choice, not an essay: lock what we are picking, put short evidence on Stage, offer two to six options with consequences, recommend one when the evidence supports it, then stop on a real choice control.
